PROJECTS


Limu and Water Quality Analysis, Chaminade University, Honolulu, HI January 2021 - Present

Collaborating with a team of students at Chaminade University to study the development and distribution of limu (Hawaiian seaweed) at Kaalawai (Cromwell’s Beach). Our research focuses on analyzing water quality and limu growth patterns, with an emphasis on understanding the impact of nutrient-rich runoff following heavy rainfall and distinguishing between native and invasive species.




Mosquito Research, UH Manoa, Honolulu, HI, May 2022 - August 2022

In the summer of 2022 I was selected to conduct research of my choice at the University of Hawaii at Manoa. I worked on my research project while also learning the cultural and spiritual prevalence native Hawaiians have with science. My research project looked at invasive Culex quinquefasciatus and how their microbiome relates to cold tolerance. This research was key to understanding effective eradication efforts of mosquitoes. Mosquitoes are invasive in Hawaii and spread avian malaria to native birds. I was able to determine that microbiome diversity leads to more cold tolerant mosquitoes and completed a research paper and I’m hoping to get published.

Scientific Storytelling, Auke Bay Laboratories, Ted Stevens Marine Research Institute, Juneau, AK May 2024 - August 2024

Conducted science communication work at NOAA’s Auke Bay Laboratories, creating infographics, videos, and hands-on tools to engage the community and educate young scientists. Led outreach efforts for key research projects, organized lab tours, and participated in community events like STEAM night. Collaborated with scientists to translate complex research into accessible formats, supporting NOAA’s mission to inform and serve the public.

Inana Innovators, Chaminade University, Honolulu, HI January 2024 - May 2024

Collaborating with business owner Lauren Roth Venu engaging in sustainable solutions to water issues stemming from Hawaii’s infrastructure. II was responsible for conducting site visits with community members communicating products and services while also incorporating meaningful insights as to why climate resilience is important. 

All-spice Research Experience, Chaminade University, Honolulu, HI October 2024 - Present

Designed and implemented a hypothesis using data collected by the University. Conducted a full analysis within R studio looking at the correlation between rainfall and water quality and seaweed presence at an ecological site.

title: Projects
text:
Here are some of my projects I have worked on!

Mosquito Research
In 2022 I had the opportunity to work in the INSTAR Lab at UH Manoa. There I worked over the summer looking at mosquito cold tolerance in relation to their microbiome. I found that males were less tolerant to cold than females and that the more diverse the mosquitoes microbiome the more tolerant they were to cold.

title: About Me
text:
Where i’m From
My name is Mehana Leafchild I was born and raised on the East side of Oahu. I love to hike, surf, paddle, run, and spend time with my family. I have grown up playing in Hawaii’s beautiful mountains and beaches. My affinity to these beautiful places have brought me to want to make a career out of protecting them. I want to preserve and protect the ecosystems, resources, and culture of Hawaii for future generations to enjoy.
